implementation_notes: Kotlin on the JVM uses java.util.ArrayDeque (a growable circular array) for the single-threaded ring and ArrayBlockingQueue for a bounded blocking queue; for a measured SPSC ring, AtomicLong with lazySet/get is the construction (the same as Java). Kotlin's contribution is minor here: the type parameter makes the element type explicit, and for a numeric ring a FloatArray/DoubleArray is the fixed, allocation-free backing store (like a typed array in JS). kotlinx.coroutines' Channel is the suspending analogue - a bounded channel suspends the producer when full rather than overwriting, which is the right choice when the producer can wait and wrong for an interrupt handler. The choice, as in Java: ArrayDeque single-threaded, ArrayBlockingQueue bounded blocking, Channel coroutine-aware, hand-written ring for a measured high-throughput path.
idiom_name: ArrayDeque / ArrayBlockingQueue / kotlinx.coroutines Channel (bounded) or a hand-written SPSC ring with AtomicLong
pitfalls: ArrayDeque is not thread-safe; use Channel or a hand-written ring for concurrent access.
Channel.send suspends when full (blocking) rather than overwriting - that is wrong for an interrupt handler and right for a coroutine; choose the policy deliberately.
The head/tail AtomicLongs may share a cache line; pad them for a real SPSC ring.
lazySet is a release store; using it for a read (where an acquire is needed) breaks the ordering.
alternative: kotlinx.coroutines Channel(capacity) when the producer can suspend and should wait rather than overwrite; ArrayDeque for a single-threaded growable ring
